findings.title: Round-3 W1's fix branch (continue-click !res.ok -> {ok:false}) has no pinning test — reverting the 413 guard ships green
findings.detail: Every wired failure test drives responder.ok:true with a failing body; the exact branch that fixed r3's 413 misrender ('Link sent' + phantom application_draft_saved) is never driven. The named regression fix of last round can be silently reverted.
findings.recommended_fix: One wiring test with responder {ok:false} asserting CONTINUE_FAILED copy, lastSentPayload NOT set (beacon still fires), and no application_draft_saved.

findings.title: Post-submit save/beacon INSERTs a fresh live draft when no row exists for (vacancy, final-email) — defeats the submit strip
findings.detail: The submitted/erased guards only fire on the ON CONFLICT branch. Applicant edits email after the last acked save and submits inside the 800 ms debounce: strip targets the final email (zero rows — no draft under it), then the pagehide beacon/second tab POSTs the same pair and the INSERT arm (cap <500) creates a fresh draft WITH PII fields and a live continue_token, submitted_at NULL. list_resumable_draft_tokens (submitted_at IS NULL AND token NOT NULL, no erased guard) lists it. Violates the strip contract 'the application row becomes the system of record'; retention sweep backstops at vacancy close. Related: carried r1-N12 (old-email draft survives strip).
findings.recommended_fix: Guard the INSERT arm against a matching submitted application for (vacancy,email), or have finalise_application strip by vacancy+any-of-the-session-emails; at minimum document the hole in the migration header.
findings.verification: confirmed (SQL read; reminder-email consequence contingent on recipient selection, not overclaimed)

findings.title: Negative-input arms on the public draft JSON endpoints untested (malformed JSON 400, invalid email on continue-link, unknown vacancy code 404)
findings.detail: P2 gap per the coverage rubric: three trivial rejection branches on unauthenticated endpoints have no test; only the /draft invalid-email twin is pinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Three small integration tests: malformed JSON -> 400 (both endpoints), invalid email -> 400 on continue-link, unknown short_code -> uniform 404.

findings.title: Stale data-resume-token references survive the r3 fix in the spec (design notes :129, review-order :261) and a draft_handler.gleam comment (:435)
findings.detail: Round 3 moved the token to window.__rtResumeToken; two current-guidance spec sections and the resumed_at code comment still describe the removed DOM attribute.
findings.recommended_fix: Update all three references to the inline-script global.

findings.title: Capability gate checks fetch/CustomEvent/JSON but the continue-click chain uses Promise.prototype.finally
findings.detail: Browsers with fetch but without Promise.finally (Edge 14-17, Safari 10.1-11.0) pass the gate; the click handler then throws synchronously after button.disabled=true — button stuck disabled, no status copy, while the save itself may already have shipped. Near-zero 2026 impact; contradicts the gate's stated ancient-browser purpose.
findings.recommended_fix: Add Promise.prototype.finally to the gate, or re-enable the button in the final .then instead.

findings.title: Permanently-unsaveable payloads (413/over-cap) retry on every step change and pagehide forever — no terminal disable
findings.detail: Only closed:true disables the saver; a 413 or field-cap rejection leaves state dirty and re-POSTs indefinitely. Silent; bounded waste. (Sibling of carried r3-N5's synchronous keepalive throw and r2-N5's 400-forever email case.)
findings.recommended_fix: Treat 413 (and 400 on the save path) as terminal for the current payload, or cap payload size client-side before send.

findings.title: 'Copy pins (sync with form_copy.gleam)' test pins only the JS half — Gleam-side drift fails nothing
findings.detail: The section name claims a cross-language sync guarantee a node test cannot enforce; the Gleam constants are unreferenced orphans (carried r2-N12), so divergence is invisible.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the Gleam constants against the JS strings in a server-side test reading both sources, or rename the JS section to what it actually pins.

findings.title: pagehide beacon ack-dedupe branch unpinned — no test asserts an acknowledged payload is not re-beaconed
findings.location: server/priv/static/form_draft.js:pagehide listener; wiring tests assert only dirty-beacon (l.249) and closed-suppression (l.242)
findings.detail: A regression costs one redundant idempotent upsert per page life — harmless server-side — but the branch exists to prevent exactly that.
findings.recommended_fix: Wiring test: ack a save, fire pagehide with unchanged fields, assert beaconCalls.length === 0.

findings.title: strip_draft_on_submit does not clear last_link_sent_at — a just-emailed-then-submitted draft occupies a fan-out slot for up to an hour
findings.detail: Erasure clears the stamp; submit does not. The 3-per-hour cross-vacancy bound counts stamped rows, so a submitted applicant's stamp still suppresses continue sends to the same address on other vacancies for <=1h. Bounded skew.
findings.recommended_fix: Add last_link_sent_at = NULL to the strip SET list (or document the deliberate difference).

findings.title: Send-failure clear drops the row from the hourly fan-out count — the 3/hour bound effectively governs successful sends only
findings.detail: During a Resend outage every retry re-claims then re-clears, so the cooldown and fan-out bounds vanish exactly when sends fail. No victim mail is sprayed (sends are failing); exposure is Resend call volume and log noise.
findings.recommended_fix: Clear to a sentinel that still counts (e.g. keep the stamp but add a separate send_failed flag), or accept and document.

findings.title: Draft strip runs before file-resolution work in finalise_application — a later failure leaves the applicant with neither draft nor a successful submit
findings.detail: Strip is deliberately fail-open so it never blocks submission, but its placement ahead of owner-resolution/uploads means a post-strip failure strands the applicant's saved answers. Retention sweep backstops; trade-off undocumented.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the strip after the last fallible step, or document the ordering rationale in the strip call-site comment.

findings.title: Resume page skips the check_max_applications gate the pristine form applies
findings.detail: A continue-link holder on a capped vacancy gets a fully restored fillable form whose submit then bounces to the closed page — wasted effort, no contract break (submit is still correctly refused).
findings.recommended_fix: Run check_max_applications in handle_resume beside is_accepting_applications, rendering the same closed page.

findings.title: PostHog session recording not explicitly disabled on the token-bearing resume page — the event-property scrub does not cover the recording pipeline
findings.detail: sanitize_properties amends event properties only; rrweb recordings are a separate pipeline. Recording is off unless enabled in PostHog project settings and capture is consent-gated (opt_out_capturing_by_default), but if recordings are ever enabled, the /resume/<token> URL lands in recording metadata unscrubbed.
findings.recommended_fix: Add disable_session_recording:true to the apply-page init config (the funnel is custom events; recording buys nothing here).
findings.verification: confirmed (init config read; claim about recording defaults matches posthog-js mechanics)

findings.title: draft_handler imports application_handler for one pure predicate — handler-to-handler import
findings.detail: is_accepting_applications is a pure predicate over GetVacancyForFormRow; reaching it couples the new module to a 2416-line handler. Housing the predicate beside the row type (application/sql) keeps handlers decoupled.
findings.recommended_fix: Move is_accepting_applications next to the row type; update both importers.

findings.title: Draft JSON handlers rely solely on the middleware body gate; no handler-level wisp body-cap pin like process_form_submission's
findings.detail: The middleware gate is real and strict (draft writes: CL required, TE rejected, 64 KB cap) — the finding is defense-in-depth only: if that wiring regresses, wisp's 8 MB default applies on an unauthenticated endpoint.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the cap in the handlers as the multipart sibling does, or leave with the middleware test coverage as the guard.

findings.title: file_slot_names() is pub with no external caller — only is_file_slot_key uses it
findings.detail: Neighbouring filter_fields documents its pub as 'pure and pub for unit tests'; this one has no consumer and no such justification.
findings.recommended_fix: Make it private.

findings.title: draft_view.view_not_found is the third near-identical token-404 page (erasure_view, dsar_view precedents)
findings.detail: Same skeleton (view_head + header + form-container/legal-document + privacy mailto), differing only in lede copy and testid. AGENTS.md's DRY rule trips at 2+.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared token-404 view parameterised on copy + testid.

findings.title: Continue-link no-leak section never tests the unknown-email enumeration path
findings.detail: The uniform-response contract (N14 anti-oracle) is pinned for the cooldown path of an existing draft; the most enumeration-sensitive case — an email with no draft at all — is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: One test: continue-link for an email with no draft answers the identical ok:true 200 envelope and creates no row.

findings.title: 120-entry cap test pins only the count; which fields survive truncation is unspecified
findings.detail: dict ordering is unspecified, so an applicant could lose first_name while field_199 survives — untested and unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin a deterministic survivor (e.g. assert email/first_name present after truncation) or sort before take.

findings.title: Exact cap boundaries unpinned: 64-char key kept, 120 kept/121 trimmed, 4000 untouched/4001 truncated
findings.detail: Tests pin only 65-dropped, 200->120, 5000->4000; an off-by-one regression escapes.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the four boundary cases.

findings.title: Cooldown pinned at 9 and 11 minutes only — the exactly-10-minutes boundary (strict <) is untested
findings.detail: A drift to <= would go uncaught at the boundary.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the 10-minutes-exact case (still on cooldown).

findings.title: F3 resume/erasure pages pin no cache-control/referrer-policy/robots headers, unlike their /erase + /dsar token-page siblings (6 pins in gdpr_integration_test)
findings.detail: Live wiring is correct (ssr_response.to_sensitive_response on the resume success render, to_not_found_response on token misses) — a wiring swap to form_view.to_html_response would silently drop no-referrer/noindex on a token-bearing page.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the three headers on the resume success page and both erasure renders.
